title: Salary Calculator Seek: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with a 38-Hour Week
description: Use our salary calculator seek to convert your hourly rate to annual pay based on a 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly estimates. Fair Work compliant.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week times 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your annual gross pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. It compensates for entitlements like paid leave that casuals do not receive. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading.

faqs.q: Does super come out of my pay?
faqs.a: No, superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings, not deducted from your pay. The rate is 12% of ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year).

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: From Hourly to Annual

If you are comparing a job offer or checking your current wage, a **salary calculator seek** can help you quickly see the full picture. Whether you are paid by the hour or offered a salary, converting between the two is straightforward when you know the standard assumptions. This guide explains how to calculate your annual gross pay, your fortnightly take-home amount, and what tax and super mean for your pocket.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

For most full-time employees in Australia, the standard week is 38 hours. That figure comes from the Fair Work Ombudsman’s definition of ordinary hours. So if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross pay is:

$30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

If you work a different number of hours each week, you can adjust the formula. But for consistency, the [the timesheet](/) on this site assumes 38 hours unless you change it. Always check your award or agreement, as some industries have different standard hours.

### Fortnightly Pay and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the example above:

Weekly pay: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
Fortnightly pay: $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00

Knowing your fortnightly amount is useful for budgeting and comparing with salary offers that are quoted per year. The [reference tables](/data) on this site include common conversions.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is $26.44 per hour. For a 38-hour week, that equals $1,004.90 per week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

However, the National Minimum Wage is a floor. Most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher rates. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page explains the difference. If you are on an award, your hourly rate may be higher than the minimum, and you may also be entitled to penalty rates, allowances, or overtime. The simple formula above does not include those extras.

### Casual Loading and Super

If you are a casual employee, your base rate is increased by 25% casual loading. That loading is part of your hourly rate, not an addition on top. When using a **salary calculator seek**, you should enter the rate you are actually paid per hour, which already includes the loading if you are casual. On this site, there is a checkbox to add 25% casual loading to the base rate you type in. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading and then tick the box – that would double-count.

Superannuation guarantee is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost to your employer. For a full-time employee on $59,280, the super contribution would be $7,113.60 per year (12% of $59,280). The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) withholds tax from each pay. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (generally). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page shows how these rates apply to your weekly or fortnightly pay.

Using the $59,280 example, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be roughly $9,088 per year, leaving about $50,192 after tax. That is an estimate only – it does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice.

### Average Earnings and Comparisons

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week (about $108,352 per year). All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week (about $82,118 per year). These are averages across all industries and states, not medians for a specific job. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page explains how to interpret these figures.

If you are looking for pay rates for a particular occupation, check the relevant award or the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page. Do not assume the average applies to your role.

### Using the Salary Calculator Seek

To get started, visit [the timesheet](/) and type your base hourly rate. If you are casual, tick the casual loading checkbox. The calculator will show your annual gross pay, weekly and fortnightly amounts, estimated tax, and super. You can also use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page to go the other way – from a salary to an hourly rate.

Remember, the results are estimates. They assume you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

### Key Points to Remember

- Annual gross = hourly × hours per week × 52. Assume 38 hours unless your award says otherwise.
- Fortnightly pay is weekly pay × 2.
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026). Casual loading adds 25%.
- Super is paid on top by your employer at 12% of ordinary earnings.
- Tax is withheld by your employer using the ATO tax tables.
- The ABS average full-time weekly earnings are $2,083.70 – but that is an average, not a median for your job.

Use the [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) on this site for more detailed information. And remember, a **salary calculator seek** is a starting point – always check your pay slip and your award for the exact figures.
